operations.summary: Enable, disable, soft-delete, queue CNAME regeneration for, or set the HTTPS protocols of websites
operations.description: Requires sites.manage and Idempotency-Key. The response preserves input order while rows are locked in UUID order. Business failures are reported per item and do not undo successful items; a database or audit failure rolls back the complete batch. Tenant principals see resources outside their active scope as site_not_found. Tenant actions against a platform-locked site fail with site_locked, while platform principals retain maintenance access. Enable performs the same local entitlement feature, state, and domains.count checks as a single website update. Disable and delete remain available while entitlement is in grace or expired state. These actions change control-plane desired state only and do not claim that an edge configuration has been activated. regenerate_cname applies only to failed CNAME allocations, requires sites.manage and dns.manage, and transactionally creates one durable CNAME job per accepted site. Its per-item result is queued; the returned site.cname_task_id is the durable task identity and site.cname_state remains pending until provider reconciliation plus authoritative and public recursive convergence completes. set_protocols (网站协议批量设置) writes basic.http2_enabled, basic.http3_enabled and basic.tls_prefer_server_ciphers of each selected site at its expected_version, as a single-site basic update would; keys left out of protocols keep each site's value. Each changed site records site.tls_profile.update, and every scope with an updated site queues its automatic publication (site.update). Its per-item result is updated.

params.name: Idempotency-Key
params.description: Stable per-actor key. Reuse with different normalized input returns 409 idempotency_conflict.

fields.description: Site IDs must be unique even when expected versions differ.

fields.name: protocols
fields.description: Required with set_protocols and rejected with every other action. An omitted key keeps each site's value; tls_prefer_server_ciphers null follows the cipher preset again.

operations.summary: Move a website to another user
operations.description: Requires sites.manage in a platform scope held by a platform administrator. In one transaction the website is re-created in the target user's tenant (new website ID, newly allocated CNAME) and the current website is deleted; the old CNAME retires by the delete rules and the customer must repoint DNS from from_cname to the new site's CNAME. Historical statistics, logs and bills stay with the previous owner. The target is another active user with a tenant of its own; target_package_subscription_id is one of that user's own package subscriptions, or null for no package. copied lists what was carried to the new website and released what the administrator must configure again; item names are http_policy, cache_policy, certificate, waf_policy, cc_policy, acl_policy, auto_defense and js_challenge (automatic DNS records are not moved). Without a carried certificate HTTPS is off on the new website. Errors: 422 site_transfer_target_invalid (target is not an active user with its own tenant, or is the current owner), 422 domain_blocked, 409 domain_verified_by_other (an apex is verified by another account, including the previous owner; domain ownership is not transferred), 409 domain_ownership_required, 409 site_locked, 409 version_conflict (stale expected_version) and 409 idempotency_conflict. Domain errors carry the refused domain and apex.
